Maya Sinha: Quick question — for the new routing fallback flow, do we show a client-facing 200 with a 'degraded' badge, or surface a 5xx/4xx with an actionable hint? I'm leaning toward 200+metadata to avoid breaking customers, but want alignment. cc @Tom Miller @Priya Rao

Tom Miller: +1 for 200 w/ explicit signal. A lot of integrations choke on non-2xx. We should add machine-readable headers like `x-redwood-fallback` and `x-redwood-degradation` and a `warning` field in the body. :thumbsup:

Priya Rao: Agree on preserving 2xx for graceful fallbacks. We still need strict 429 semantics when it's quota/capacity; Retry-After must be set there. For fallback-to-smaller-model, suggest this body pattern: ```json
{"status": "degraded", "warning": "Response may be lower quality; a fallback model was used.", "fallback_model": "rw-small-v1"}
``` Also add a telemetry tag `degrade_reason`.

Ben Carter: Console UX note — add a yellow 'Degraded' badge for routes that have recent fallback traffic, and show per-request badges in traces with a tooltip: "fallback model used / quota throttled / regional failover." Also surface a tiny quality diff sample (orig vs fallback) in the route dashboard to help product owners.

Tom Miller: Telemetry needs fields: `degrade_reason` (quota|capacity|model_unavailable|region), `degrade_action` (fallback|queue|reject), and `degrade_model` when applicable. We should codify a mapping table:
- quota -> 429 + Retry-After header
- capacity shortfall -> prefer 200+status: degraded when fallback is used; if no fallback, 503 with `retryable: true`
- model crash -> 500 with `retryable: false`

Maya Sinha: Proposed contract for API v2 (non-breaking):
1) Transparent fallback: HTTP 200, response body includes `status: \"degraded\"` and `warning`, headers `x-redwood-fallback`, `x-redwood-degradation` (soft|hard).
2) Quota exceeded: HTTP 429, include `Retry-After` and `x-redwood-quota-remaining` header.
3) No fallback available & transient infra: 503 with `retryable: true` in JSON.
4) Terminal errors: 500 with `retryable: false`.

This keeps SDKs simple: default SDK layer treats `status: degraded` as success, but surfaces a `degraded` flag to callers and increments a metric.

Priya Rao: Small API example for SDK helpers: ```js
// sdk: normalize response
if (resp.headers['x-redwood-degradation'] === 'soft' || resp.body.status === 'degraded') {
  resp.normalized = { ok: true, degraded: true, fallback: resp.body.fallback_model };
} else if (resp.status === 429) {
  throw new QuotaError(resp);
}
```

Ben Carter: UX followups: add console filter for "degraded" traffic, show % of requests in last hour that were degraded, and a small alert if >5% for a route. Also add explainer copy: "Degraded = fallback model or reduced capacity used; quality may be affected."

Tom Miller: One more: ensure we emit a sampling of full request/response pairs (with PII redaction rules) when degradations happen so evals can auto-detect regressions. Tag sample events with `degrade_sample=true`.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: rollout/degrade-badging v1 -> staging at 2026-03-20T22:00:00Z by @Ben Carter

Priya Rao: I'll write the RFC for header names, exact JSON fields, and SDK mapping today. Action items: Priya = RFC, Tom = telemetry schema update, Ben = console badge + samples prototype. Maya = final decision and announce on next eng sync.

Ben Carter: ack — will push a mock to staging and link in the RFC when done.
